DEZINERSKNOT / BUSINESS ANALYSIS & PRODUCT DELIVERY

Dezinersknot

Making freelance agreements work, from proposal to payout.

I clarified business requirements, evaluated payment options, coordinated provider onboarding and tested marketplace workflows.

THE CORE DESIGN CHALLENGE

How could clients and designers agree on scope, payment and review terms that the marketplace could actually support?

PROJECT FACTS
MY ROLEBusiness analysis, UX refinement and UAT
TIMELINEJan 2025–Oct 2026 · BA focus from Jul 2026
COLLABORATIONProject manager, business, studio, development, QA, accounts, legal and providers
DELIVEREDRequirements, provider onboarding support and a UAT tracker
MARKETPLACE JOURNEY

Two sides of one agreement.

Clients need clear scope and payment terms. Designers need clear requirements, timely reviews and a route to payout.

The opportunity

The client publishes project requirements, deliverables and budget expectations.

The negotiation

Designers submit proposals. Payment preferences and contractual expectations may differ between the parties.

The commitment

The client offers a contract. The designer can accept, propose edits or decline. Revised terms may require another decision before agreement.

The delivery

The designer submits work. The client reviews it, and approval, inactivity, disputes and payout rules determine what happens next.

01 / 04
PROJECT BRIEF

Make the agreement work through delivery.

Dezinersknot connects clients with freelance designers. The business team owned commercial decisions, and the external studio created much of the original interface. My role was to clarify requirements and help the teams carry them into delivery.

THE UNDERLYING UX PROBLEM

Both parties need to know what they’ve agreed to, who acts next and what happens to the money if work changes, stalls or is disputed. Each decision has to stay consistent from proposal to payout.

PAYMENT CHOICES

Feedback changed the payment options.

Feedback raised a need for full-project funding. Reusing a single milestone was simpler to consider, but could imply staged funding where the parties intended one payment.

I gathered internal feedback, clarified payment requirements, assessed the trade-off and discussed proposed refinements with the studio using AI-assisted prototypes.

Separate options make the terms easier to understand. The clearer choice introduces additional payment logic, which the team had to weigh against reusing milestones.

Feedback came through Microsoft Forms and direct conversations. Overlap is unverified, so the counts should not be added together.

AGREEMENT & EXCEPTIONS

Where an agreement can break down.

Clients and designers can prefer different terms. After submission, inactivity or disagreement can leave the next action and payout unclear.

I clarified negotiation states and explored how each party could see the other’s payment preference without adding more fields to the form. I also helped define proposed review and exception rules.

Revised contract terms need another decision. Work submission starts review, and a dispute needs a separate path before settlement.

Evidence and limits The proposal included a seven-day inactivity condition and a fourteen-day period with an unconfirmed trigger. Final approval and implementation of the exception and refund-credit rules remain unverified.

Narrowing the wallet to refund credits

The broader proposal gave users a general wallet balance. That raised questions about how the marketplace would hold and manage funds. I recommended limiting credits to refund-related use and taking the proposal through legal and business evaluation.

PROVIDERS & PAYOUTS

Getting from payment to payout.

Provider and bank requirements limited the intended fund handling. Collecting client payments and releasing designer payouts also required different controls.

I researched provider options. Razorpay was easier to adopt and provided stronger support in the team’s experience. An HDFC-related constraint on the intended fund-handling arrangement led the team to pursue Cashfree despite a more involved onboarding process.

Evidence and limits The documented MVP specified administrator-triggered bank payouts after applicable approval. Live escrow and later payout automation remain unverified.

What I coordinated with accounts and legal

I worked across accounts, legal and Cashfree to move the application through documentation and verification. I submitted the required corporate documents, including the Memorandum of Association (MOA), followed up with the provider and supported payment and payout testing.

  1. Coordinate the application with accounts and legal
  2. Submit corporate documents and support verification
  3. Follow up with Cashfree and support transaction testing

How commission changed for both sides.

I analyzed commission alternatives alongside provider costs and constraints, verification, payout operations and relevant tax and accounting considerations. The business approved the revised fee model.

TESTING & DELIVERY

Turning test findings into team action.

Payment retry dialogs, proposal empty states and unclear form content needed reproducible reports before the team could act.

I tested workflows, filed Plane tickets, discussed priorities with the project manager and developers in stand-ups, and coordinated follow-up and retesting.

Recording the expected behavior and reproduction context helps the team decide what to fix and verify what happens afterward.

OUTCOMES & REFLECTION

The experience depends on the decisions behind it.

My work connected feedback and requirements with provider onboarding, testing and delivery coordination.

What I contributed

Feedback synthesis, UX recommendations, requirements analysis, commission comparisons and coordination across the project team.

What was delivered

Documented payment and review requirements, provider application and verification support, and a regression tracker with 139 observations for follow-up.

What is not verified

Production behavior for proposed dispute and refund-credit rules, payout automation, exact timing conditions and post-launch gains in conversion, satisfaction or revenue.

What I learned

Even a small change to payment or review can change who owns the next decision and what operations must support.

Dezinersknot sharpened how I approach marketplace work. Every promise in the interface needs an owner and a workable process behind it.
